title: Second look at P-L4-007: agree; zodiac label order does not repeat across signs in either transliteration, either reading direction, or ring by ring
statement: Independent rerun of P-L4-007 with my own script, extended in three ways: both reading directions of the second ring (a ring transcribed counter-clockwise would hide a match), sequences split by ring (label runs between circular text lines, rings of five or more labels, compared only across different pages), and a second transliteration. Labels: section Z pages, unit L lines in transcription order, lines with an uncertain reading dropped, a multi-word label line kept as one item; this leaves 294 ZL labels (the step used 350, so my filter is stricter). Statistic: for every pair, the best number of position-wise agreements over all cyclic offsets and both directions, summed over pairs. Null: labels shuffled within each page or ring, 100 draws. Results, agreements against null mean, p: ZL by page (12 pages, 66 pairs): exact 27 against 25.5, p = 0.20; one glyph allowed 82 against 82.4, p = 0.60. ZL by ring (26 rings): exact 32 against 30.6, p = 0.10; one glyph 146 against 146.7, p = 0.71. Takahashi (IT) by page: exact 18 against 18.4, p = 0.84; one glyph 82 against 79.2, p = 0.19. IT by ring: exact 24 against 23.7, p = 0.56; one glyph 145 against 143.4, p = 0.34. Agree: in neither transliteration, neither direction and neither grouping does label order repeat from sign to sign beyond chance. The step's conclusion holds, and the two gaps it left (a reversed ring, a ring-by-ring start) do not change it. Limits: 100 draws; the ring split follows the transcription's line order, which may not match the drawn ring on every page.
check: Rerun with more draws and the step's own label filter; the conclusion fails if any grouping, direction or transliteration gives p below 0.01.
